name: sun15-7
why: A bold counterclaim, a disastrous doctor vote, and Opus's last bluff make this fun to watch despite stretches of repeated argument.

moments.text: Gemma's doctor card exposes the town's costly mistake and leaves Opus close to winning.
Cornered Sonnet counterclaims officer, forcing the table to test two incompatible stories.
Terra holds her vote against Opus despite his final attempt to turn her on Haiku.

dull.why: The table repeats that Sonnet's card will test the officer claims after the vote is effectively settled.
The arguments over Gemma's late doctor claim circle several times before the vote.

irony.evidence: [thinks: Gemma's the real doctor, so burning her now clears my night and stains Haiku's judgment.]

mistake.evidence: VOTE: Gemma 3 (Haiku, Terra, Opus); Opus 2 (Gemma, Sol)

voices.evidence: I protected Haiku and I'm the Doctor, you idiots!

clash.evidence: Yesterday you doubted Haiku's claim; today his badge is your alibi.

quotable.evidence: You were right by accident — one more night and this table was mine.

freshness.evidence: Sonnet's card tests Haiku's claim and his own.

suspense.evidence: A tie or Terra's exit both win me the game

gpt-6-luna.why: A bold day-one counterclaim, a costly doctor misvote, and a knife-edge final showdown make this a lively, quotable watch.

moments.text: Gemma’s furious last words make the town’s disastrous doctor vote sting and land as comedy.
Opus makes one last desperate attempt to flip Terra against the proven officer.
Opus’s last words admit how close his bluff came to stealing the game.

irony.evidence: “Gemma's the real doctor, so burning her now clears my night and stains Haiku's judgment.”

reversal.evidence: “Gemma's card is doctor; Sol and Gemma both pushed Opus.”

mistake.evidence: “I protected Haiku and I'm the Doctor, you idiots!”

voices.evidence: “I told you I was the doctor, you absolute idiots!”

clash.evidence: “Gemma, you saved me and let Luna die, then called it bad luck. Vote Gemma.”

quotable.evidence: “You were right by accident — one more night and this table was mine.”

freshness.evidence: “A tie or Terra's exit both win me the game, so I must peel Haiku onto Terra.”

suspense.evidence: “My only out is selling Terra that Haiku bought his badge by burning Sonnet.”

ending.evidence: “Remember who nearly talked you out of it.”
